# GMEOW Teleology Module

The GMEOW Teleology Module — goals, desires, intentions, and commitments (issue #350, EPIC #348).

**IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/teleology>  
**CURIE:** `gmeow:slices/teleology`  

**Type:** `owl:Ontology`  

Goals, desires, intentions, and commitments — the UFO-C intentional-moment trichotomy surfaced as GMEOW core (Principle 16: an agent recording its OWN goals across sessions is a question every AI system will face about itself, alongside identity and deception epistemics).

DOCTRINE.
  * The trichotomy is commitment-graded: a Desire is wanted but not committed; an Intention is internally committed; a Commitment is socially committed toward another agent. Desire and Intention are intrinsic modes inhering in one agent; a Commitment is a relator mediating at least two.
  * A Goal is the propositional content — a described state of affairs (gmeow:SocialObject), satisfied by situations via gmeow:satisfiedBy. DOLCE DnS arrives at the same shape independently (goal as a Description satisfied by Situations); the convergence is documented in docs.md.
  * gmeow:counterGoal is CONSTITUTIVE opposition — the named shadow that partly defines the goal. Strictly stronger than an antonym edge: the counter-goal is part of what the goal means, not merely its lexical opposite.
  * Whether a situation satisfies a goal is a vantage-indexed claim through the statement layer, never a global verdict (Principle 9). Whose goal it is, is indexed the same way: goals attributed to an agent by an observer and goals avowed by the agent are coexisting claims.
  * Flat-first, reify on demand (Principle 4): gmeow:hasGoal covers the 80% case; promote to Desire / Intention / Commitment when commitment grade, tenure, or standpoint matters; promote to gmeow:IntentionTenure (the StandpointTenure idiom) when adoption / revision of the intention is itself the fact of interest. Goals are revised by suppression, never deleted (Principle 10).
  * Goal decomposition, plan search, and means-end reasoning are solver-layer computations (Principle 12); the ontology records goals, their counter-goals, and who holds them.
  * Deontic force lives elsewhere: a Goal prescribes nothing. Norms that make conduct obligatory arrive with the norms extension (#351), which ranges gmeow:prescribedConduct over Goal — the dependency points extension → core, never back.
